# Widget profile 1

*Generated by `packages/core/scripts/profile-build.ts` from `packages/core/profile.json`; do not edit. Frozen 2026-10-17: 279 features, 201 in, 78 out.*

The profile is the contract between widgets and clients: a feature is **in** when every client draws it the same way, and every client's
validator removes what is **out** before it reaches the renderer, so a widget looks the same on iOS, Android, macOS, desktop and the web.
The validator (`packages/core/src/host/validator.ts`, `css-sanitizer.ts`), the Swift node model (`NativeValidator`), the sandbox shim and
the renderer read their tables from this profile (`src/shared/profile-tables.ts`); `packages/conformance` checks a client against it.

## Detecting the profile

- `TelegramWidget.profile` is `1`; `TelegramWidget.isProfileAtLeast(n)` is `profile >= n`. A later profile only adds features.
- `CSS.supports(property, value)` and `CSS.supports(condition)` answer from the profile: `true` only when the validator keeps the declaration as written.
- `@supports` is evaluated by the validator against the same tables: the block is kept (unwrapped) or dropped before the CSS reaches the renderer.
- A widget that checks nothing still loads; what is out is removed, as described in the tables below.

## Decisions

| key | decision |
|---|---|
| D3 | A feature is in when every client draws it; :hover and user-select: text are the exceptions (progressive enhancement: where a client lacks them, the widget still works) |
| D3a | v1: canvas 2D; Web Animations, filter, backdrop-filter if clients draw them; out: forms, inner scroll, 3D transforms, magic move; CSS animations and transitions in |
| D3b | Fonts: system generic families only, other names dropped |
| D4 | Input: taps in the PoC, drag in v1; no keyboard at all, not even Enter or Space (it conflicts with the chat input field; Artem, 2026-10-16) |
| D5 | strict policy everywhere; webAnimations and morphUpdates from the profile |
| D6 | 3D (__tw3d) cut from the release |
| D8 | SDK outward: openLink (confirmed with the full URL) and openTelegramLink (no confirmation of its own, 2026-10-29) on a tap, haptics; no sendMessage |
| D11 | One widget model: classic DOM in the sandbox |
| D12a | Above the cap: hard clip, no fullscreen |
| D14 | Theme: themeParams + --tg-theme-*, theme change event |
| D17 | State: localStorage per (account, chat, message id): the chat the message is in, as message ids are unique only within a chat (supergroups); 4 KB, QuotaExceededError; sessionStorage in memory |
| D18 | Text is not selectable by default; a widget enables selection with user-select: text (2026-10-20, replaces "Text selection forbidden") |
| D20 | Mini-HTML (2026-10-17): a widget is one HTML document of at most 4 KB compressed and 32 KB uncompressed, delivered in the message; the server compresses the HTML from the bot (zlib at level 9 since 2026-10-24) and enforces both limits |
| D21 | No accessibility in v1 |
| D23 | Runtime profile detection: TelegramWidget.profile / isProfileAtLeast, CSS.supports and @supports from the profile |
| inv1 | Invariant 1: widget JS only in QuickJS |
| inv2 | Invariant 2: the host validates everything against the allowlists |
| inv4 | Invariant 4: only data: images, host blob: and #fragment URLs reach the renderer |
| inv5 | Invariant 5: no network in QuickJS |
| inv6 | Invariant 6: navigation cancelled, shadow scope |
| P1 | Profile v1 freeze (2026-10-17): a candidate is in when the corpus uses it and the web renderers draw it; the rest are out until the native renderers are measured (profile 2) |
| P1-grid | Grid is in on condition that the Swift renderer and TwidgetCore implement it before their releases (2026-10-17) |
| P1-libs | No bundled libraries in v1 (2026-10-17) |
| P1-ua | Clarified in v0.1.1 (2026-10-20): the renderer's user-agent layer (tables.uaStylesheet) also fixes the root and the text elements: the bubble's text colour (the bubble's own fill is the canvas behind a transparent renderer), the client's text tokens (--tg-text-font-size, --tg-text-line-height, --tg-text-padding as the body's margin) and explicit sizes and margins for headings, paragraphs, lists, tables, quotes and code, so a UA default in this profile means that layer, not an engine's own stylesheet |
| SDK | SDK v1 (docs/sdk-v1.md), with Artem's answers of 2026-10-17: haptics without a gesture (bucket 5, 10 per second), any t.me path, URLs of at most 256 characters, 16 handlers per event type, stopped after 2 crashes in a row, double tap and long press stay with the bubble (replaced by G1 in v0.1.2) |
| G1 | Gestures, v0.1.2 (Artem, 2026-10-22): one shared policy with the same thresholds on every client and in the sandbox. A double tap over the widget is always the widget's (both clicks and dblclick, on every element; the reaction stays with the bubble outside the widget). For the rest touch-action is the claim, decided per element at pointerdown over the target and its ancestors (a container covers its children, as in CSS): auto: holds and swipes are the bubble's (the widget gets pointercancel); pan-y / pan-x: drags on the other axis are the widget's; none: everything is the widget's, holds (contextmenu) included. The leading 20 px of the widget and the bubble outside it never take a claim. Replaces "double tap and long press stay with the bubble" (SDK) |
| G2 | Vertical drags are the chat's, v0.1.3 (Artem, 2026-10-24): a widget claims only horizontal drags; a vertical drag over a widget always scrolls the chat, whatever touch-action says, and the widget gets pointercancel. auto: holds and drags are the bubble's; pan-y: horizontal drags are the widget's; pan-x claims nothing; none: horizontal drags and holds (contextmenu) are the widget's. The axis lock (the first move past the 10 px slop decides for the whole press), double taps and the leading 20 px are unchanged. The engine under the renderer always allows vertical panning. Replaces G1's pan-x and the vertical half of none |
| R1 | Resize anchor, v0.1.3 (Artem, 2026-10-24): TelegramWidget.setResizeAnchor('top' \| 'bottom') says which edge of the bubble stays put on screen when the widget's height changes (top by default: it grows downward; bottom: it grows upward and the content above moves). An SDK v1 addition inside profile 1: TelegramWidget.profile stays 1 and widgets detect the method with typeof. It goes through the bridge as a checked call (sdk-policy, four copies and the fixture), needs no gesture, and the host keeps the latest value and reports it with the height; the client's list compensates its scroll |
| I1 | The bot's data and requests (Artem, 2026-10-25; the server's spec): a widget is fixed code plus changeable state: the HTML never changes after sending; the state changes, and only the bot writes it. TelegramWidget.chatData, the chat state (one original message, seen only in its chat: in a group every member sees it; never forwarded), and publicData, the shared state (wherever the widget is shown: a forward gets a copy, or shares a shared widget's one state with the original): each a text of up to 1024 bytes (UTF-8), read-only in the widget; chatDataChanged / publicDataChanged when they change (no restart). isForward, chatType and viewer (Mini Apps' WebAppUser: id, first_name, last_name, username, is_premium; a field that breaks its rule is left out); a forward is told nothing about the chat it is in (no chatType: the bot must not learn where its widget was forwarded), and the widget knows its viewer only where it may ask the bot (can_query), originals included. request(data of 1-64 bytes): a callback button inside the widget; where it may ask is the server's per message (can_query: originals of a widget sent with allow_queries, forwards of one sent with fwd_allow_queries; background_query: the original in the private chat with the bot); the client marks a widget with can_query as one whose tap may send data to the bot's server; on a tap, one per tap (shared with openLink, openTelegramLink and copyText); in the background while visible: one when the widget appears on screen, then one per 5 s; one in flight; resolves { result } (text of at most 1024 bytes), rejects with error.code; the answer does not change the state. copyText(text of 1-256 characters) on a tap; the client's toast shows what it copied. Part of SDK v1 and layer 233 from the launch, inside profile 1. TelegramWidget.isPreview: an inline result in the list before it is sent gets its state but no input, no bridge call but ready and setResizeAnchor, no chat type or viewer, and Web Storage that is never committed. The checks are sdk-policy (four copies and the fixture) |
| L1 | Strict limits from the start (2026-10-29): about twice what real widgets use; past a counted cap the widget stops (docs/decisions.md) |
| L2 | Heavy boxes (Artem, 2026-11-02, after the client teams' stress-kit runs on five devices): at most 16 heavy boxes at once (a blurred box-shadow layer, a filter, a backdrop-filter, opacity below 1 but a disabled or pressed <button>'s, or a running animation of filter, backdrop-filter or opacity, or of box-shadow through a blurred layer), of them at most 2 with backdrop-filter; every renderer counts on the computed style (packages/core/src/shared/paint-policy.ts and its fixture) and past either the widget stops. A tightening of profile 1 (widgets were not launched yet), not profile 2 |
| P1-safe-area | Clarified on 2026-10-29 (Artem; widgets were not launched yet), not profile 2: a client draws the message time and its status over the bottom corner of a widget with no caption below it, as on a photo (with a caption below the time is in the caption's line and nothing is drawn over the widget; a caption shown above the widget, invert_media, is as none: Artem's decision of 2026-10-30). env(safe-area-inset-top\|right\|bottom\|left[, fallback]) is in: the validator rewrites it to var(--tg-content-safe-area-inset-…[, fallback]), root variables the renderer sets like the theme's (bottom = the height of the time's band, the others 0), with --tg-content-safe-area-corner-left\|right for the width of the client's corner in that band (a physical side: right in a left-to-right interface, left in a right-to-left one); 0 with a caption below. Another env() name resolves to its fallback or drops the declaration. The UA layer adds the band to the body's bottom padding, and TelegramWidget.contentSafeAreaInset with the contentSafeAreaChanged event gives the same numbers to script |

| `sel.host-scoped` | :host, :host-context(), ::slotted(), ::part(), :scope | **out** | the selector never matches (dropped from its list) on every renderer | inv6 |
| `sel.target` | :target | **out** | the selector never matches (dropped from its list) | P1 |

## Limits

| id | feature | status | when out | decision |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `limit.text-node` | Text values (text node, canvas string, Path2D data) up to 32 K UTF-16 units; past it the widget stops (strict) | in |  | D5 |
| `limit.text-budget` | Document text 48 K units, past it the widget stops; complex-script text 8192 units, past it the text is refused (strict) | in |  | D5 |
| `limit.nodes` | At most 2000 nodes (elements, text, comments) in the document once a batch is applied; past it the widget stops (strict) | in |  | P1 |
| `limit.timers` | At most 64 live timers (RangeError past it) | in |  | P1 |
| `limit.cpu` | CPU quota 300 ms of JS per second (timers deferred, not killed; a task that runs past it makes the next ones wait longer); one task may run 500 ms; at most 128 layout queries in one task, and their time at most 1000 ms; past these the widget stops | in |  | P1 |
| `limit.memory` | QuickJS heap 8 MB | in |  | P1 |
| `limit.storage` | localStorage 4 KB per message (QuotaExceededError) | in |  | D17 |
| `limit.attribute` | Attribute and inline-style values up to 8 K UTF-16 units; past it the widget stops (strict) | in |  | L1 |
| `limit.batch` | At most 10 000 operations in one batch (the shim hands a task's DOM changes over in batches of about 1000, its element method calls in one); past it the widget stops (strict) | in |  | L1 |
| `limit.css-rules` | At most 400 CSS rules and 32 @keyframes in the document's stylesheets; past them the widget stops (strict) | in |  | L1 |
| `limit.canvas-commands` | At most 4000 canvas commands per canvas in one task (RangeError past it; strict) | in |  | L1 |
| `limit.animations` | At most 64 running script animations (further ones are not rendered; strict) | in |  | L1 |
| `limit.main-thread` | The host's main-thread work for a widget, its layout queries plus 25 µs per operation and 2 µs per canvas command, at most 100 ms per second (timers and frames deferred past it) | in |  | L1 |
| `limit.canvas-pixels` | A widget's canvases hold at most 2048 × 2048 pixels together; past it the widget stops (strict; the renderer itself never applies a size past 4096 × 4096) | in |  | L1 |
| `limit.paint-heavy` | At most 16 heavy boxes at once: a blurred box-shadow, a filter, a backdrop-filter, opacity below 1, or a running animation of one of them (shadows animated without blur do not count, nor the opacity of a disabled or pressed <button>: its own dimming); elements under display: none and a ::before / ::after without content are no boxes; past it the widget stops (strict; every renderer counts on the computed style) | in |  | L2 |
| `limit.paint-backdrop` | Of the heavy boxes at most 2 with backdrop-filter; past it the widget stops (strict) | in |  | L2 |
| `limit.image-pixels` | A data: image of at most 1024 × 1024 pixels, as its bytes say (larger: the placeholder); bytes of none of the profile's image formats are a broken image | in |  | L1 |
| `limit.html-size` | HTML up to 32 KB uncompressed and 4 KB after zlib compression (server-side) | in |  | D20 |
| `limit.url-length` | openLink / openTelegramLink URLs of at most 256 characters (TypeError past it) | in |  | SDK |
| `limit.event-handlers` | At most 16 handlers per event type in onEvent (more are ignored) | in |  | SDK |
| `limit.haptic-rate` | Haptics: a bucket of 5 calls refilled at 10 per second, and a touch: free while a finger is down on the widget and 5 s after it is lifted, otherwise one 1 s series (the next after a touch or 10 s later); the rest dropped (haptic-limit) | in |  | SDK |

## Client behaviour

| id | feature | status | when out | decision |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `behaviour.theme-switch` | Live theme switch: prefers-color-scheme, light-dark() and onTheme follow the chat theme without a reload | in |  | D14 |
| `behaviour.offscreen-pause` | Off-screen: frames stop, timers at most 1 Hz, visibilitychange fires | in |  | P1 |
| `behaviour.auto-height` | The bubble takes the widget height; above the cap it is clipped hard | in |  | D12a |
| `behaviour.no-selection` | Text is not selectable by default (a drag over text selects nothing); user-select: text enables it | in |  | D18 |
| `behaviour.policy-strict` | strict policy on every client (gesture gate, text caps, budgets) | in |  | D5 |
| `behaviour.restart` | After 2 consecutive crashes the widget stays stopped on its last frame with the "Widget stopped" badge; before that the client rebuilds it when shown again | in |  | SDK |
| `behaviour.gesture-claim` | touch-action is the claim: taps and double taps over the widget are always its own, vertical drags always the chat's; auto leaves holds and horizontal swipes to the bubble (the widget gets pointercancel); pan-y gives the widget horizontal drags; none gives it horizontal drags and holds; pan-x claims nothing; the leading 20 px and the bubble outside the widget never take a claim | in |  | G2 |
| `behaviour.storage-persist` | localStorage survives the widget being dropped and re-created, and an app restart; sessionStorage survives re-creation but not a restart; both are deleted with the message | in |  | SDK |
| `behaviour.storage-forward` | A forwarded copy has its own storage, keyed by its own chat and message, so it starts empty | in |  | SDK |
| `behaviour.message-edit` | The HTML of a sent widget never changes (an edit may change only the caption): a bot changes only the widget's state, chatData and publicData (behaviour.data-edit) | in |  | I1 |
| `behaviour.size-hint` | Before load the bubble takes the bot's size anchors (width 0 = the bubble's width, W = a fixed width in [200, max]; height 0 = the placeholder, then the content height in [50, 600]; H = a fixed clamp(H, 50, 600)), cached per message | in |  | D12a |
| `behaviour.time-corner` | A widget with no caption below it (none, or one shown above it) gets the message time and status over its bottom corner, on a backing as on a photo, and taps on it are the client's; the client passes the band (contentSafeArea bottom) and its corner (cornerRight, or cornerLeft in a right-to-left interface) before the first render and changes them only with the bubble's layout (a caption added, removed or moved above or below by an edit, "edited"); with a caption below the time is in the caption's line and the safe area is 0 | in |  | P1-safe-area |
| `behaviour.resize-anchor` | When an auto height changes, the client keeps the widget's anchored edge in place on screen: top (default), the content below moves; bottom, the content above moves; also from a cached height and after a re-creation | in |  | R1 |
| `behaviour.data-edit` | A change of the widget's state reaches the running widget as chatDataChanged / publicDataChanged (the client's setData with the full state: the server's update, or the polled shared state): no new host, no restart | in |  | I1 |
| `behaviour.forward-copy` | A forwarded copy never has a chat state (chatData); its shared state (publicData) is a copy as of the forward or a shared widget's one shared state; it is told nothing about the chat it is in (no chatType); it asks the bot only on a tap and only if the widget was sent with fwd_allow_queries, and otherwise has no viewer either | in |  | I1 |
| `behaviour.preview` | A widget in a list of inline results is a preview: the client creates it with context.preview and the result's state, routes no touches to it (a tap selects the result) and creates a new host for the sent message | in |  | I1 |
| `behaviour.network-marker` | The network marker: the client marks a widget whose tap may send data to the bot's server exactly where the message has can_query (a UI contract of the server's spec) | in |  | I1 |

## Tables

What the validator lets through; anything else is removed as the features above say.

- **HTML elements kept:** `a`, `abbr`, `address`, `article`, `aside`, `b`, `blockquote`, `body`, `br`, `button`, `canvas`, `caption`, `cite`, `code`, `col`, `colgroup`, `data`, `dd`, `del`, `details`, `dfn`, `div`, `dl`, `dt`, `em`, `figcaption`, `figure`, `footer`, `h1`, `h2`, `h3`, `h4`, `h5`, `h6`, `head`, `header`, `hgroup`, `hr`, `html`, `i`, `img`, `ins`, `kbd`, `li`, `main`, `mark`, `menu`, `nav`, `ol`, `p`, `picture`, `pre`, `q`, `s`, `samp`, `search`, `section`, `small`, `span`, `strong`, `sub`, `summary`, `sup`, `table`, `tbody`, `td`, `tfoot`, `th`, `thead`, `time`, `tr`, `u`, `ul`, `var`, `wbr`.
- **Rendered as `<span>`:** `bdi`, `bdo`, `big`, `font`, `label`, `legend`, `nobr`, `output`, `rp`, `rt`, `ruby`, `strike`, `tt`; **as `<div>`:** `center`, `dialog`, `form`; unknown elements: `<span>`.
- **Dropped with their subtree:** `applet`, `area`, `audio`, `base`, `datalist`, `embed`, `fencedframe`, `fieldset`, `frame`, `frameset`, `iframe`, `input`, `link`, `listing`, `map`, `math`, `meta`, `metadata`, `meter`, `noembed`, `noframes`, `noscript`, `object`, `optgroup`, `option`, `param`, `plaintext`, `portal`, `progress`, `script`, `select`, `set`, `slot`, `source`, `template`, `textarea`, `title`, `track`, `video`, `xmp`.
- **HTML attributes:** `class`, `id`, `title`, `lang`, `dir`, `hidden`, `role`, `colspan`, `rowspan`, `span`, `width`, `height`, `alt`, `open`, `start`, `reversed`, `datetime`, `value`, `type`, `disabled`, `style`, the URL attributes `href` and `src` (checked), and the prefixes `data-*`, `aria-*`.
- **SVG elements:** `svg`, `g`, `path`, `rect`, `circle`, `ellipse`, `line`, `polyline`, `polygon`, `text`, `tspan`, `defs`, `symbol`, `use`, `linearGradient`, `radialGradient`, `stop`, `title`, `desc`, `a`.
- **SVG attributes:** `class`, `id`, `lang`, `role`, `viewBox`, `preserveAspectRatio`, `x`, `y`, `x1`, `y1`, `x2`, `y2`, `cx`, `cy`, `r`, `rx`, `ry`, `d`, `points`, `dx`, `dy`, `rotate`, `transform`, `width`, `height`, `fill`, `fill-opacity`, `fill-rule`, `stroke`, `stroke-width`, `stroke-opacity`, `stroke-linecap`, `stroke-linejoin`, `stroke-dasharray`, `stroke-dashoffset`, `stroke-miterlimit`, `opacity`, `color`, `display`, `visibility`, `overflow`, `text-anchor`, `dominant-baseline`, `alignment-baseline`, `baseline-shift`, `font-family`, `font-size`, `font-weight`, `font-style`, `letter-spacing`, `word-spacing`, `text-decoration`, `gradientUnits`, `gradientTransform`, `spreadMethod`, `fx`, `fy`, `fr`, `offset`, `stop-color`, `stop-opacity`, `pointer-events`, `shape-rendering`, `text-rendering`, `vector-effect`, `paint-order`, `cursor`, `pathLength`, `version`, `xml:space`, `xml:lang`, `href` (fragments only).
- **Image types (`data:` URLs):** `image/png`, `image/jpeg`, `image/jpg`, `image/gif`, `image/webp`.

- **Element methods that reach the renderer:** `setPointerCapture`, `releasePointerCapture`, `scrollTo`, `scrollBy`, `observeResize`, `unobserveResize`; properties: `scrollTop`, `scrollLeft`.
